title: Dramatis snapshot document
description: A character relationship graph derived from a narrative work, bound to the exact text and the exact analysis that produced it. Deliberately medium-neutral: nothing in this schema names a unit of any particular form. Structural position is an ordered path of typed segments whose types are supplied per work.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of this schema that the document was written against.

id.description: A stable identifier, unique within its kind in this document.

provenance.description: Where a claim came from. 'observed' means the narrative text enacts it. 'asserted' means the author stated it in reference material outside the narrative. 'human' means a person entered or corrected it in the application.

reviewStatus.description: How far a claim has travelled through human review. Corrections must survive re-analysis.

collection.description: A set of related works sharing one character registry. A standalone work is a collection of one.

work.description: A single narrative body within a collection.

segment_types.description: Ordered vocabulary of structural segment types used by locators in this work, outermost first. Supplied as data, never fixed by this schema, so any medium can be addressed. Example: ["part", "section", "paragraph"].

edition.description: Free-text edition identifier, for collections holding several editions of one work.

document.description: One file within a corpus. A work may be a single document or many.

path.description: Path relative to the corpus root, if the document came from a file.

role.description: 'narrative' documents enact the story and yield observed relations. 'reference' documents describe it from outside and yield asserted relations.

textRevision.description: An immutable, content-hashed state of a work's text. One of the two axes a snapshot is bound to.

label.description: Human-facing name for this revision, supplied by the user.

sha256.description: Hash over the normalised concatenation of the revision's documents. Two revisions with the same hash are the same text.

analysisRun.description: One execution of the extraction pipeline. The second axis a snapshot is bound to. Recorded in full so a result can be cited and reproduced.

model.description: Provider-qualified model identifier as reported by the provider.

prompt_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the extraction prompt text as sent. prompt_version is a label a human maintains and may stay put across an edit; this is the prompt itself. Two runs whose hashes differ were given different instructions and are not comparable as analyses of the same text, whatever their versions claim.

parameters.description: Sampling and decoding parameters as sent to the provider.

snapshot.description: A graph produced by binding one analysis run to one text revision. Immutable. The two axes stay separate so a change can always be attributed to the text or to the analysis, never ambiguously to both.

segment.description: One step in a structural path. 'type' is drawn from the work's declared segment_types and is data, not an enumeration.

index.description: Ordinal position among siblings, counting from 1.

label.description: The segment's own name, where it has one.

locator.description: A position within a work, expressed as an ordered path of typed segments from outermost to innermost.

selector.description: A quotation with surrounding context, after the W3C Web Annotation TextQuoteSelector. Lets evidence be re-anchored once the underlying text has been edited, which character offsets alone cannot survive.

exact.description: The quoted text, verbatim. Must be found in the source or the extraction is rejected.

start.description: Character offset into the revision's normalised text. A hint for fast lookup, never the authority.

evidence.description: A passage supporting a claim, anchored so it survives revision of the text.

note.description: What this passage shows about the claim.

character.description: A node. Identity is stable across snapshots so that graphs may be diffed.

name.description: The form used to label the node.

aliases.description: Other surface forms resolved to this character, including assumed names and titles.

salience.description: Relative prominence within the work, 0 to 1.

relation.description: An edge. Weight drives rendered thickness and is meaningful only against its declared basis.

directed.description: False for mutual relations. True where the relation runs one way, such as one character concealing something from another.

weight.description: Closeness of the relationship, on the scale named by weight_basis.

weight_basis.description: What the weight counts. Weights are comparable only within a shared basis, so this is required and must be carried through every export.

types.description: Free-text relation types, e.g. "kinship", "antagonism", "alliance". Deliberately not enumerated: no closed vocabulary survives contact with real narrative.
